findings.title: Persisted source/output closure oracle is not independently asserted
findings.detail: The positive owner test reads only S21 revision and S22 row count before publication. Returned hashes are carried directly into PublishReady, and logs print owner-returned outcomes. The packet requires exact persisted hashes, references, roles and artifact closure derived from actual immutable inputs; the current test does not independently reconstruct and compare these persisted values. Actual T3 success exercises the current guard, but cannot independently detect a shared preparation/publication derivation mistake.
findings.required_change: Read complete persisted S15/S16/S21/S22/S23/S24/S25 provenance, basis references and policy role/artifact closure; independently reconstruct source, projection/dependency, candidate and artifact hashes from those immutable inputs and assert exact values and references.

findings.title: Denial snapshots do not prove zero changed rows
findings.detail: state(preparation=True) stores the full S01 row but only counts the preparation, publication, receipt/event/outbox and authority tables. Most basis, identity and candidate denials compare this snapshot. A denial that modified an existing candidate/history/receipt/event row while keeping counts unchanged would satisfy these assertions, contrary to the required zero new rows/changed rows and immutable-history oracle.
findings.required_change: For each required denial compare stable complete row snapshots, including S21/S22/S23 and relevant S02/S03/S04/S24/S25 and authority rows, before and after; retain existing S01 comparisons and real owner-driven races.

findings.title: Duplicate contenders lack exact persisted cardinality/history assertions
findings.detail: The tests correctly establish local contention with bounded Events and pg_blocking_pids, then assert identical contender outcomes. They do not explicitly inspect the new S21 row and complete S22 closure, new S23 row/candidate, or unchanged previously committed preparation history after each duplicate race. Equal returned IDs alone do not fulfill the packet oracle of one immutable result/dependency closure/build with no overwrite.
findings.required_change: After each projection/build/completion race assert exactly one corresponding persisted S21/S23 identity, exact complete S22 semantic keys and references, unchanged immutable payload/candidate bytes, and zero unintended authority/receipt/event/outbox changes.

review_scope: T3-PREPARATION immutable S21/S22 creation and exact local S23 BUILDING-to-READY completion
T3 publication current-basis/registry/time rechecks and shared S51 -> S01 ordering preserved
Exact SHA/resolved-root lifecycle validation before nested destructive operations

observations: pg_blocking_pids confirms projection/build advisory contention and S23 completion row contention
Real owner-produced SEALED S15 -> atomic immutable S21/S22 -> locally completed S23 -> actual T3 publication
Injected failures after S21, midway S22, before/after READY, and after T3 S01 update fully roll back
Historical replay is byte-identical and does not repoint later published S01 head
S01 blocker does not block preparation; no S01/S51 preparation relation locks; unchanged actual T3 ordering and stale-basis denial

limits: Hosted legacy PostgreSQL/quality and selected-task merge gates remain coordinator pre-merge obligations; no legacy/default DB fixture was run locally.

All independent selectors and full suite pass, but existing assertions do not yet satisfy the three exact packet oracles identified above. No transaction implementation flaw was demonstrated by this review.
